topic: RACOON-RAVEN: what the code does, chain of proof, screens and walkthrough
summary: RACOON-RAVEN turns uploaded CSV/XLSX tables, including a column with whole report texts, into filled study templates with one record per patient and timepoint. Every source writes a proposal with its cell or its quoted passage; the server checks that the quote is really in the text (exact except case and whitespace, first occurrence), and values that only a model read always wait for a person or a bulk accept. Conflicts, flags, a field history and a trace of every model call make a value checkable back to the uploaded row. The chain ends there: there is no PDF or ORBIS connection, a found quote does not prove that the value is right, and missed values leave no mark. Code state: main a7fa7ec, 2026-11-22; read, not run.

concepts.name: Study
concepts.plain: One research project that holds visits, forms, patients, inputs and records.

concepts.name: Timepoint
concepts.plain: One planned visit, for example T0 baseline or T1 follow-up, optionally with a day offset and a window.

concepts.name: Template
concepts.plain: The empty form: questions with type, unit, allowed answers and a hint for the model. Stored as a FHIR R4 Questionnaire with draft, active and retired versions.

concepts.name: Patient / subject
concepts.plain: One person of the cohort with a study pseudonym and, for matching, name, birth date, sex and identifiers.

concepts.name: Input
concepts.plain: One uploaded CSV or XLSX sheet. One of its columns may hold full report texts.

concepts.name: Mapping
concepts.plain: Which column answers which question, which cell words mean which answer option, and which column is the report text.

concepts.name: Match review
concepts.plain: A queue for rows whose patient or timepoint is not certain. A person decides.

concepts.name: Record
concepts.plain: One filled form: one patient, one timepoint, one template.

concepts.name: Proposal
concepts.plain: What one source says about one question, with the place it came from. Several can stand side by side.

concepts.name: Field state
concepts.plain: proposed, auto accepted, accepted, corrected or rejected.

concepts.name: Conflict
concepts.plain: Usable sources disagree, or new evidence disagrees with an earlier decision.

concepts.name: Flag
concepts.plain: A proposal with a defect: quote not found, value needs mapping, invalid value.

concepts.name: Reference date
concepts.plain: A date of the record. Sources can be sorted by how many days they are away from it.

concepts.name: Trace
concepts.plain: The stored questions to and answers from the language model for one row.

concepts.name: Export
concepts.plain: CSV or XLSX, one row per record, with value, state and source per question, plus a code book.

pipeline.what: Create study, timepoints, template (editor or Questionnaire JSON import) and cohort (import wizard).
CSV or XLSX only, first row is the header, at most 10,000 rows and 500 columns. File goes to object storage with SHA-256, each row is stored as raw cells.
Four steps: keys, columns, values, summary. Suggestions come from the server, a person saves. A report text column and a strategy can be chosen.
Background job sends each report text with the question list to the configured model and stores value plus quotes per question.
Pseudonym, then patient ID, contradictions refused; fuzzy matches only as suggestions. Timepoint by code, date window or fixed.
Cells and model answers become proposals; the state of the field is derived from them.
Accept, correct, reject, reopen per field; conflict view; bulk accept of agreeing values; record closes when nothing is open.
Value, state, source per question; optional choice of the document closest to a reference date; code book and documents export.

provenance.how: Unique per input row, question and method (mapping or llm); stores value, raw text, location, flags and, for llm, the run.
provenance.limit: Reprocessing updates or deletes proposals in place (services/ingest.py:176-195); older proposal states are not kept.

provenance.how: Mapped values store column name and row number plus the raw cell text.
provenance.limit: Blank rows are dropped before numbering (services/cohort_file.py:90, services/inputs.py:204), so the number can differ from Excel. Dates and whole numbers are normalised on reading (cohort_file.py:76-86).

provenance.how: JSON schema requires value and a list of verbatim, contiguous quotes for every question; null is allowed.
provenance.limit: Providers that refuse the schema get plain json_object for the rest of the job (llm/client.py:82-84). No confidence score.

provenance.how: Substring search after collapsing whitespace and folding case, mapped back to offsets in the original text. Not fuzzy. First occurrence.
provenance.limit: Proves presence of the words, not that they support the value. Short quotes can point to the wrong occurrence.

provenance.how: Set when no quote of the answer was located, including an empty quote list. Flagged proposals never auto-accept, never count for agreement and keep the field open.
provenance.limit: One located quote is enough; additional invented quotes only get a small marker. A reviewer may still accept a flagged proposal (field_state.py:54-61).

provenance.how: Values are coerced to the type of the question; unknown model codes become invalid_value.
provenance.limit: No plausibility ranges. Conversions by the model (cm to mm) are not recomputed.

provenance.how: All unflagged proposals agree and at least one is a mapped cell. Model-only values stay proposed.
provenance.limit: A single mapped cell satisfies this rule alone; no second source and no human look is needed.

provenance.how: Raised when unflagged proposals differ. Human decisions are not overwritten; later disagreement raises the conflict again.
provenance.limit: Until decided, the field shows the oldest value (mapping first). Flagged proposals do not raise a conflict.

provenance.how: Open means conflict, or only proposed, or undecided with a flag. A record cannot be closed while a field is open and reopens on new evidence.
provenance.limit: Empty fields are not open. A record can be reviewed with values the model missed. Auto accepted values need no look.

provenance.how: Accepts every agreeing, unflagged proposed field in the current filter and names the user in the history.
provenance.limit: Includes model-only values nobody looked at; stored reason review:bulk_accept is not shown in the UI history (frontend/src/lib/records/format.ts:68-72).

provenance.how: One event per state or value change with from, to, value, user, time and reason.
provenance.limit: Does not store the chosen proposal. Record-level close and reopen are not events (review.py:163-180). Append-only by convention; no trigger found.

provenance.how: Run: model, host, strategy and version, template version, text SHA-256, status. Step: messages, schema, raw answer, error, duration, tokens.
provenance.limit: Shown on the input page per row, not linked from a field. Retries, fallback mode, model weights hash and reasoning are not recorded.

provenance.how: Sort sources by signed days between document date and a reference date; the export can settle open conflicts with the closest document.
provenance.limit: Depends on a date column in the table. In the review it only sorts; in the export it can pick a value without a human decision (state stays proposed).

provenance.how: Document ID, else filename:row, or manual for a free correction.
provenance.limit: No quote, offsets, model, reviewer or time. Empty if the proposal behind an accepted value was withdrawn. Contains unreviewed values with their state.

provenance.how: Auto accepted, accepted and corrected values are written to a QuestionnaireResponse.
provenance.limit: No provenance in it; status is always in-progress (line 48).

provenance.how: Uploaded file kept in object storage with SHA-256.
provenance.limit: No code reads it back or rechecks the hash; the viewer sees stored cells. The clinical document behind the table is not linked.

gaps_vs_notes.code: Only as text in a CSV/XLSX column or one pasted report (needs a configured provider). No PDF, DOCX, scan or OCR; explicitly out of scope in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-llm-ingestion-design.md section 0; parser refuses other files (cohort_file.py:30-37).
Yes, one sheet per input, header in the first row, one row per patient/timepoint or per letter.

gaps_vs_notes.note: Link with a structured report template
gaps_vs_notes.code: Yes, FHIR R4 Questionnaire. Mapping is suggested, a person saves it.
It fills proposals. Values only read by a model stay proposed until a person accepts (singly or in bulk). Mapped cells without disagreement are accepted automatically.

gaps_vs_notes.note: UI shows where a value comes from
gaps_vs_notes.code: Yes: cell highlight and marked quote in the text stored with the row. Not in the original PDF or in ORBIS; there is no ORBIS connection.
No such template in the repository (tracked text files searched). Only the invented CT thorax staging template.

screens.name: Record page
screens.why: Core picture: source left, form right. Click a field: its cell gets an aqua border, its quote turns from yellow to solid aqua and scrolls into view. Click a marked passage: the field that quoted it is selected. Best traceability moment.

screens.name: Conflict view
screens.why: One disagreement at a time: one card per distinct value with file, row, document ID, date, distance and the quote in its sentence. Keys 1 to 9 decide.

screens.name: Mapping wizard
screens.why: Shows how a table meets the form: columns linked to questions, one column marked as report text.
screens.evidence: frontend/src/routes/studies/[id]/inputs/[inputId]/+page.svelte (steps Keys, Columns, Values, Summary; text column at 599)

screens.name: Trace
screens.why: The exact question to the model and its exact answer, with model, duration and tokens.

screens.name: Records list
screens.why: Overview for the patient by timepoint grid with open, auto accepted, proposed, decided, conflict and flagged counts; filter 'needs attention'.

screens.name: Template editor
screens.why: Optional: item tree, preview and the extraction hint per question, which makes the expert's definition visible.

walkthrough.title: Start with the question, not the document
walkthrough.viewer_sees: Empty form 'CT thorax staging' with four sections; the hint at tumour size: largest axial diameter in mm, no lymph nodes, no prior values.
walkthrough.spoken_point: The researcher decides what to ask and how it is defined. The form comes first.

walkthrough.title: Put the hospital's table in
walkthrough.viewer_sees: baseline.xlsx drops in. Lines connect columns to questions; the column 'Befund' (report) gets the mark 'report text'.
walkthrough.spoken_point: The usual Excel list and the free text travel together. No PDF yet: the text must already be text.

walkthrough.title: Every source makes a proposal
walkthrough.viewer_sees: Form of invented patient LC-009, T0 fills. Examination date: cell and text agree, green 'auto accepted'. cT stage T2, contrast yes, no distant metastases: yellow 'proposed' with LLM tag.
walkthrough.spoken_point: What only a model has read is never accepted by itself.

walkthrough.title: Click a value, see the proof
walkthrough.viewer_sees: Click on 'T2'; in the report 'cT2a' turns from yellow to aqua. Staged variant: the model's quote is not in the text, red tag 'quote not found'.
walkthrough.spoken_point: The system searches the quote itself. If the words are not in the letter, it says so.

walkthrough.title: Two sources disagree
walkthrough.viewer_sees: Conflict cards (order may vary): 48 mm, baseline.xlsx, Tumorgröße (mm), row 10; 38 mm, LLM, '...Raumforderung im linken Oberlappen, 38 mm...'. The 38 mm card is accepted. History: proposed to accepted, name, time.
walkthrough.spoken_point: Most likely a typing error in the list. Without the second source nobody would have noticed. A person decides and signs.

walkthrough.title: From the table back to the sentence
walkthrough.viewer_sees: Export row: 38 | accepted | baseline.xlsx:10. Arrow back to record, quote, report. Then the Trace with the exact question and answer of the model.
walkthrough.spoken_point: Chain of proof: number, decision, passage, document row. Proven: the words are there. Judged by a person: what they mean. Not covered: what was overlooked.

demo_setup: Python 3.14, uv, Node 24, Docker Desktop, just, Git Bash. cp .env.example .env; just infra-up; just install; just migrate; just dev (API 8000, worker, frontend http://localhost:5173, Keycloak 8080, dev user 'annotator' in infra/keycloak/racoon-realm.json). There is no seed script: follow the click path in samples/lung-ct/README.md (study with T0/T1, import template, cohort.xlsx, baseline.xlsx, followup.xlsx). Extraction needs a local OpenAI-compatible model via RR_LLM_BASE_URL and RR_LLM_MODEL; sample README measured about 7 s per report without thinking and 90 s with (qwen3.5-9b). frontend/e2e/fake-llm.mjs is a fixed-rule stand-in for layout only. Not started or tested for this note.

llm_and_data_flow.provider: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint from server settings; no default URL or model; off without both; temperature 0; timeout 120 s; concurrency 2
llm_and_data_flow.data: Full report text is sent unchanged to the configured endpoint. Local operation is possible (Ollama, llama.cpp), not enforced. No de-identification. Prompt and text are stored in the trace.
llm_and_data_flow.auth: Keycloak OIDC, RS256 JWT; no roles, no study membership
llm_and_data_flow.privacy: Per-study pseudonyms, but names, birth dates and IDs are stored and exported (services/export.py:361-377). UI loads fonts from Google Fonts (tokens.css:6).

upstream.checked: page and README read via web; gh not installed
upstream.what: RAVEN, Radiological Analysis and Validation Engine with NLP; MIT; FastAPI, Postgres, Svelte; extracts fields from free-text radiology reports and lets people rate them; Ollama or OpenRouter; single API key; research artifact, not a medical device
new: proposals from several sources, conflicts, flags
upstream.paper: Römer et al., RAVEN: An open-source assessment framework for automated entity extraction in structured radiology reporting, Informatics in Medicine Unlocked 63, 101755 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.imu.2026.101755. Search snippet only (publisher 403): 5,355 items rated by two medical researchers, 11 error categories, Mistral-24B better than Llama-70B by 22.6 %. Not results of RACOON-RAVEN.

maturity.evaluation_figures: No extraction accuracy recorded in the repository

limits: A found quote proves that the words are in the text, not that they support the value.
First occurrence only: a short quote may be marked at the wrong place.
One mapped cell alone is accepted automatically, without a second source or a human look.
Values the model misses leave no mark; empty fields are not open; completeness is not checked.
Bulk accept can accept model-only values nobody looked at.
The history does not store which proposal was chosen; proposals change in place on reprocessing.
The chain ends at the uploaded row. Original PDF or ORBIS document is not linked; stored original file is not shown.
Row numbers can be off when the file has blank rows.
Export has no quote, reviewer or model; it contains unreviewed values and identifying patient data.
Auto accepted and accepted share the same green; only the word differs.
No de-identification before the model call; where data goes depends on the configured endpoint.
No accuracy figures for RACOON-RAVEN; not a certified medical device (inferred from upstream wording, no statement in this repository).
